facts.premium: Highest mainland-South pay tier — Hat Yai commerce, the largest factory base in the region, and a more formalised economy.
facts.skill_gap: Better skilled-labour supply than the deep south, but still a large informal majority outside Hat Yai/industry.
anchors: Hat Yai commerce, retail and cross-border trade (Malaysia)
Largest factory & seafood-processing base in the South (~74k workers)
workers: Hat Yai traders, retail and service workers
impacts: ~74k factory workers give Songkhla the South's strongest formal-income base — steadier collateral underwriting.
Cross-border Malaysian trade and commerce drive a deeper, more diverse credit market.
Rural districts still depend on rubber, so commodity swings move part of the book.
High car and EV counts (top in the region ex-Phuket) widen ticket sizes upmarket.
Proximity to the conflict provinces can dampen activity in southern districts.
Hat Yai is the most contested lending market in the South — margin and acquisition pressure.
